column2: A Solarque Reborn

After decades of submission under the reign of foolish heathens, the Soleil Royal faith has restored its original splendor and luminous glory. Thanks to many worthy conquests in the name of [sun_king_cultist.GetHighGodName], the partisans of the Diable have been pushed back to lands not graced by his luminous kingship of the newly anointed Solarque.
Long live the Solarque!
That is none of our business.
Foolish heathens, God will punish them!

Your might and majesty as the [ROOT.GetPrimaryTitles] has lead priests thorughout the [sun_king_cultist.GetName] world as a great leader blessed by [sun_king_cultist.GetHighGodName] himself. Some even wonder if you might share the blood of the blessed Sun King...
Let us investige this!
This is foolish

A pile of texts have been gathered to trace back your bloodline through the generations. The task will take weeks, and you wonder: do you lead the search youself, or pass the responsibility on to [ROOT.job_spiritual.GetName]?
I will do it myself!
[ROOT.job_spiritual.GetFirstName] will do a fine job!

After weeks of study, you have found it! A missing link tying you to a bastard son of the mighty Sun King himself! The priests and scholars of the land have all verified this ancestry. The old Capet families may seethe in private, but all true followers of [sun_king_cultist.GetHighGodName] acknowledge your claim.
Praise [sun_king_cultist.GetHighGodName]!
Weeks of searching and stress have lead to nothing. The threads you traced back generations, all the work of your scholars, and no connection to the Sun King to be found.
Curses!

Your valiant deeds have become known by many throughout the [chevalier.GetName] world. Many priests and kinghts have begun to speak of you in reverent tones, hailing you as a Worthy, a knight whose valor and virtues are fit for comparison to those of the Nine Worthies of Old.
I hope that I prove worthy of this honor

A wandering knight has arrived to my court, drawn in by the tales of my virtue and valiance. [invited_character.GetSheHeCap] claims to have traveled far and wide, searching for a liege worth following, and that [invited_character.GetSheHe] wishes to pledge [invited_character.GetHerselfHimself] to my service.
I will give you command of an army.
I am sorry, but my court is full.

A wandering bard has arrived at my court, drawn in by the great tales of my valor and honor. [invited_character.GetSheHeCap] claims that [invited_character.GetSheHe] wishes to pledge [invited_character.GetHerHis] loyalty to me and sing about the great deeds of my dynasty.
You are welcome!

I have received a distraught message from a damsel in need. [From.GetTitledFirstName] is suffering under the yoke of an uncouth [From.Liege.GetManWoman] with no honor. Hearing tales of my valor and my status as a Worthy Knight of the Chevaliers, [From.GetSheHe] pleads me to offer [From.GetHerHim] my protection.
Fear not, my [From.GetLordLady]! I will protect you!
Unfortunately, I cannot offer assistance now.

After a long week on the road, I have arrived at the castle to deliver [event_target:damsel_in_distress.GetTitledFirstName] from [event_target:damsel_in_distress.GetHerHis] captors. Soon, I am faced with the commander of guard, who has heard the tales of my skill in combat. He agrees to release [event_target:damsel_in_distress.GetTitledFirstName] if I can defeat him in a duel.
Alright then! En Garde!
On second thought, I better head home...

While the duel was hard-fought, you have emerged as the victor. [event_target:damsel_in_distress.GetTitledFirstName] falls into your arms, thanking you endlessly for taking [event_target:damsel_in_distress.GetHerHim] away from this dreaded place.
You have been defeated in the duel and must ride home to your castle in shame, without rescuing [damsel_in_distress.GetTitledFirstName].
My Lady! May I have your hand?
You will be welcome to stay in my court
I will never live this down...

While once you were once known for valor and virtue, your dishonorable behavior has become too apparent. The priests who once spoke of you as a Worthy now spit at the mention of your name. At least for now, your time in their favor is over.
I ought to look over my sins.

The ever-present shadow of disease and pestilence still plague your kingdom. Your subjects again cry out to see you work miracles with your healing royal touch. As their [From.GetTitle], it is time for you to fulfill your duty and bring healing to the sick with your blessed hands. Your healing powers are important for your legitimacy in the eyes of the priesthood and your subjects.
The loyal [royal_touch_vassal.GetTitledName] needs my blessing.
[royal_touch_courtier.GetFirstName] shall have my blessing.
I will bless the scrofula patients in [royally_touched_province.GetName].
Your liege [from.GetTitledFirstName] has heard of your illness, and is on the way to give you his royal touch..
Praise [sun_king_cultist.GetHighGodName]!

You greet [royally_touched.GetFirstName] with the clergy and physicians accompanying you. Couriers and common folk flock around you, looking up in awe at your royal presence. They witness you give the weakened & sickly [royally_touched.GetFirstName] your blessed touch.
May this touch heal you from your ills...
Your gracious liege [from.GetTitledFirstName] arrives at your court, and blesses you with his royal touch.
May my lord's touch cures me from my disease.
[From.GetFirstName] has not showed signs of recovery from their diseases despite the royal touch you gave [From.GetHerHim] recently. Some traitors are even beginning to doubt your power.
Curses!
[from.GetFirstName] has sent you a letter full of praises. It seems that your touch was successful as your vassal has fully recovered from [From.GetHerHis] illness after you touched [From.GetHerHim].
[sun_king_cultist.GetHighGodName] blesses me with the Divine Rights to Rule!

You decide to head out to the hospital in [royally_touched_province.GetName] with your royal clergy and physicians accompanying you. The scrofula patients wait in line for your royal touch to heal them, each one covered with repulsive lesions. Bystanders crowd around you as the afflicted subjects wait for your blessing. You begin blessing your patients one by one as they line up for your healing touch.
May these poor souls be cured from their illness with my touch.
Reports from the hospital you visited in [royally_touched_province.GetName] are full of excitement. Many of those you blessed with your touch earlier have now fully recovered!

In spite of your royal blessing, it seems your subjects have not shown any signs of recovery from their illness, with some even dying afterwards. While many of your lowal followers argue there must have been a mistake, some traitors are beginning to doubt whether {sun_king_cultist.GetHighGodName] still blesses you with the divine right of royalty.
[Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] blesses me with the Divine Rights to Rule.
Curses!
Worthy
The [chevalier.GetName] priesthood has recognized this character as a truly worthy and valiant knight for whom other chevaliers will flock to [this.GetHerHis] banners.
Blessed Hands
The people has recognized the King as having hands that are capable of blessing the sick from illness.
Shamed Knight
This Knight has lost [this.GetHerHis] position as a Worthy Knight of the [chevalier.GetName] Faith, a great shame for [this.GetHerHim] and all thier blood-kin.
Both characters follow the [chevalier.GetName] Religion.
Claimed Capet Bloodline
This character has found a claim to the holy blood of the Capets, bringing glory to his name and enraging the previous families to claim descent from him

Musketeers

The legends of the Musketeers, warriors who fought for the king through thick and thin, were and remain very popular in France. Who hasn't heard of the heroism of D'Artagnan, Athos, Aramis, or Porthos? Today, the Musketeers still exist—training and honing their skills in combat and virtue. Although the musket has been forgotten, the values of honor, loyalty, and piety have not been forgotten.
Monsieur
Chevalier
Mousquetaire
Grand-Croix
Madame
Chevalier
Mousquetaire
Grand-Croix
Restore The Order of the Star

Long ago, there existed the Order of the Star (Ordre de l'Étoile), a chivalric order founded by a French king, whose knights swore allegiance to Dieu and their king and never to flee the battlefield. Perhaps now is the time for Solarque to revive this noble order.

The Order of the Star, known in French as the Ordre de l'Étoile, had just been founded by Solarque. At its inauguration, the first friars swore allegiance to Dieu and their Solarque from that day until the end of their days, and that they would never flee from the battlefield, but would either win or die on it. Although the formal purpose of the order is to protect pilgrims and abbeys, whispers of other uses for this order are already being heard.
Ordre de l'Étoile
The pride of our faith!
The false believers are arming themselves...
Ordre de l'Étoile is created...
Go on Le Pelerinage

In ancient times, many holy knights and virtuous ladies made Le Pelerinage, a pious pilgrimage to the pleasant places of [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName]—to atone for their sins and gain new merits. Are you planning to do the same?
Le Pelerinage

There comes a time in the life of every devotee of Le Dieu Solaire when they begin to think about Le Pelerinage—a pious, walking journey once practiced by the knights of Le Roi Soleil and their equals in piety and loyalty. These journeys took place to many places, but some time after Louis Laflamme's martyrdom, it became commonplace that Le Pelerinage could take place either in the Vendée, or in Reims, or in Paris or Aachen. These places were considered by the spiritual descendants of the martyr-king Laflamme to be dear to [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName], Jesus, and La Vierge Reine, and vibrant with the divine spirit. Now that you have chosen Le Pelerinage, you must also decide which direction you will take.
To the Vendée, the land of most loyal
To Paris, the Heart of the Kingdom
To Reims, the place of coronation of the kings
To Aachen, home of Charlemagne

After preparing for your journey, you finally set off for your Le Pelerinage. You dress in beggar's clothing. As you emerge from behind your estate, you encounter the abbot, who blesses you and says, "May [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] support you on your pilgrimage to the heart of the kingdom dear to him there, his eldest daughter and the jewel of his heavenly crown," before anointing himself with holy oil. As you continue your journey, you reflect on what Paris means to your faith and how much the Church of Saint Gertrude there or the suburban Louvre mean.

After preparing for your journey, you finally set off for your own Le Pelerinage. You dress in beggar's clothing. As you emerge from behind your estate, you encounter an abbot who blesses you and says, "May [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] support you on your pilgrimage to the place where so many martyrs rose against Usurpateur and the demonic Marianne, and shed their blood for the rightful kings," before anointing himself with holy oil. As you continue, you contemplate the history of the Vendéen uprisings against the cruel Robespierre and the usurping Napoleon.

After preparing for your journey, you finally set off for your Le Pelerinage. You dress in beggar's clothing. As you emerge from behind your estate, you encounter an abbot who blesses you and says, "May [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] support you on your pilgrimage to the place where Saint Jeanne d'Arc, La Vierge d'Orléans, brought about the coronation of the rightful King of France against the blasphemous usurpation of Albion," before anointing yourself with holy oil. As you continue your journey, you reflect on what Paris means to your faith and how much the Cathédrale Notre-Dame de Reims there means.

After preparing for your journey, you finally set off for your Le Pelerinage. You dress in beggar's clothing. As you emerge from behind your estate, you encounter the abbot, who blesses you and says, "May [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] support you on your pilgrimage to the place where the holy emperor, Rex Ambulans, sat as if on his throne, and from there oversaw the prosperity of France," before anointing himself with holy oil. As you continue, you ponder the events that Aachen Cathedral witnessed—the reign of the holy emperor Charlemagne, but also the fall of the Carolingian dynasty.
[Root.Religion.GetHighGodName], protege-moi dans ce voyage!
Goal of Le Pelerinage

You enter the destination of your Le Pelerinage — Paris, the heart of the former Kingdom of France and the Ancient Régime. It was from here that Le Roi Soleil, Henri the Great, reigned, and here that King Louis suffered martyrdom, murdered at the instigation of the demon Marianne by her minions: Danton, Marat, and Robespierre. You walk through the streets of Paris and see people of all appearances: the poor and the rich, locals and visitors, pilgrims and sinners. Soon, passing by all these people, you reach one of the places worth seeing—the square where King Louis suffered martyrdom, of which even his killer said: "He was too good not to forgive me." You gaze at this place with bliss and pay homage to the martyred king by removing your hat.

You reach the Vendée, this beautiful land that nurtured so many martyrs and knights who fought for the kingdom of France against the minions of the demon Marianne and the usurpers who roamed the French lands. You observe these farms, the farmers working valiantly, and the mothers tending their livestock. The ancestors of these people, though members of the Third Estate, also did what those born higher up did, for they betrayed their king and God. You decide to stay in this land for a while, to see the old battlefields and cementaries, to remember the martyred knights of Bonchamps, Charette, and Cathelineau.

You reach Reims, the city where King Charles, the rightful king of France, was crowned during the Hundred Years' War, fighting against English usurpers and the arrogance of Albion. As you pass through the streets of this magnificent city, you glimpse the Cathédrale Notre-Dame de Reims in the distance. Soon you reach it and enter. You see that despite much devastation and desecration by worshippers of the demon Marianne, this church has retained its splendor. You imagine King Charles being crowned in this temple to defy the English usurpation, accompanied from afar by Jeanne d'Arc, the Maid of Orleans, the king's faithful subject, but also a holy martyr.

You arrive in Aachen, the city where Charlemagne, the greatest and first king of France and Holy Roman Emperor, reigned and led his empire. Here, just laws were enacted and people were judged according to the highest standards. You wander the streets of Aachen and notice that no one speaks the language you know, but somehow you manage to communicate with one of the locals, who leads you to the Cathedral – you wander through it, sensing the sacredness of this place. After a while, you reach the palace chapel, where Charlemagne always heard mass. You stand there, kneel, and begin to pray.
Dieu, entends...
Crying Youth

Passing near a certain town, you hear a faint cry by the river. Curious, you investigate and see a young man sitting by the river with a sword, dressed as if he were a poor nobleman. You strike up a conversation with him and he tells you that he's fallen in love with a girl, the daughter of the local mayor. At times, she seems to show him favor and genuinely enjoy his presence, and at other times, she treats him like air, even shuns him as if he were a leper. He doesn't know what to do about it, because he feels that she loves him deep down, though sometimes he feels otherwise, making his life disgusting and unsure of what to do with him.
Advise him to propose to her, time of her charades will be ended...
Advise him to go with you instead of her....
Advise him to ask his confessor about this matter...
You leave without a word, such conversations delay your journey....
I'll give him some advice on communicating with women...
You say what you wanted to say. After a moment, the man thanks you for your advice and wishes you luck on your journey, then walks away toward his village.
I also wish him good luck...
Peasant Letter

An employee of your office brought you a strange letter today—without a seal and written in a very clumsy hand. He was about to throw it away, but something compelled him to bring it to you. You thank him and read it. You learn that the author is a certain young man. After a moment, you remember the young man you met by the river during your journey to the holy place. In this letter, he writes that his courtship ended in failure, and due to his poor decisions, he lost his fortune and became a drunkard begging in a town near your lands. He asks you for help, as he pleads that he will die soon and is nearing the end of his days. You decide to help him. You order your servants to locate the young man and give them coins to give to him.
Sad story...

An employee at your office brought you a strange letter today—without a seal and written in a very clumsy hand. He was going to throw it away, but something compelled him to bring it to you. You thank him and read it. You learn that the author is a certain young man. After a moment, you remember the young man you met by the river during your journey to the holy place. In this letter, he writes that his advances ended in failure and even a certain humiliation, but he eventually rose from them, and certain circumstances caused by his unsuccessful advances fortunately formed an opportunity that yielded him a considerable profit and allowed him to live a decent life. Although you are saddened that he failed, you are glad that he didn't end up in a bad mood because of it and lives happily, despite not winning the heart of the girl he loved.
The bittersweet ending to this story...

An employee at your office brought you a strange letter today—without a seal and written in a very clumsy hand. He was going to throw it away, but something compelled him to bring it to you. You thank him and read it. You learn that the author is a certain young man. After a moment, you remember the young man you met by the river during your journey to the holy place. In this letter, he writes that he has won the heart of the woman he loved. Your heart rejoices, but then you read on, and the joy leaves you. He writes that his wife is a torment to him, that she reproaches him all day long, that she hates him, that her decision to marry him is the worst of her life, and that he expects that in a few days his wife will leave him with the children and expose him in his home village as a failure (which, by the way, he believes he is), a bad husband who was unable to make his wife happy or earn a living. You smell alcohol from the letter, which makes you even sadder...

An employee at your office brought you a strange letter today—without a seal and written in a very clumsy hand. He was going to throw it away, but something compelled him to bring it to you. You thank him and read it. You learn that the author is a certain young man. After a moment, you remember the young man you met by the river during your journey to the holy place. In this letter, he writes that he has won the heart of the woman he loved. Your heart rejoices, but as you read on, the letter fills you with even greater joy. The letter's author has fathered several children with his beloved, and thanks to the support of the girl's father, his business is doing very well and he expects great profits in the coming years. At the end, he thanks you for your advice and tells you that he, his wife, and their children pray for you daily in his prayers.
Nice, Happy End happened...

An employee of your chancellery brought you a strange letter today—without a seal and written in a very clumsy hand. He was going to throw it away, but something urged him to bring it to you. You thank him and read it. You learn that the author of the letter is a certain young man. After a moment, you remember the young man you met by the river during your journey to the holy place. He writes in this letter that his confessor advised him differently than he wanted, but he listened and entered the monastery and gained the education needed to heal people. Today, he is asking for permission to enter your court so that he can preach the faith as a monk and heal people, including you.
I will gladly welcome him to my court...

You come across some peasants singing a strange song about Saint Guinefort. You've never heard of this saint, so you stop for a moment and listen to the song from afar. But the peasants notice you and recognize you as a stranger, then call out to you to join them.
I'm joining them
I ignore them and move on.
Saint Guinefort

You join the peasants. You reveal that you are on your own Le Pelerinage and are journeying to a sacred place. They greet you even more cheerfully and begin to tell you the legend of Saint Guinefort. Saint Guinefort was a dog who lived long ago. A snake attacked his master's child, and the dog defended him by biting him to death and covering himself in blood. When his master returned, he found the dog with blood in his mouth in front of the cradle. He assumed the child had killed him and killed him. Realizing his mistake, he buried the dog with honor. Since then, Saint Guinefort has been a folk saint, whom the peasants pray for healing and protection for their young children.
Interesting myth...

When you finish listening to the legend of Saint Guinefort, the peasants sing another song about this dog. You spend the rest of the day being entertained by the nearby peasants, given food and drink. The old men learn the songs of Saint Guinefort and only let you go after you recite one to them.
Intersting people...

As you walk, you come across a group of musicians singing a beautiful song you know well: it is a song about Saint Roland, the martyr knight and nephew of Charlemagne, who represented the knightly virtues so praised by your religion.
Listen their ballade...
Ignore them and move on

As you walk, you encounter a troupe of musicians and singers. They sing a ballad about the wars in Italy, when the kings of France fought against the Spanish, Albion, and Germans for dominance in Italy. You hear stories of the martyred knights of Pavia, the brave defenders of Boulogne against the tyrant king Henry VIII, and other heroes of those wars.
Beautiful ballad of great deeds...
Or maybe it is peace, it is better than the most beautiful wars....
As you walk, you suddenly see two drunken renegades in front of you with drawn swords, who have a clear intention towards you.
Time to fight!
Dark Forest

While hiking, you pass through a dark forest. You walk and walk, and just when you think you're finally out, you realize that where you'd hoped to exit the forest, there's no exit. You feel lost. It's dark, and you can hear every animal nearby. You feel stressed by this situation and try to find some landmarks. Just when you think you're lost to the wolves, you see two silhouettes in the distance, holding lanterns. You call out to them, and although they initially seem to be moving away, they turn back. After a moment, you see them clearly, they're monks.
Thank Dieu, there weren't wolves with lanterns in their mouths...
Monastery

The monks lead you to their monastery, telling you its history along the way, and in return, you tell them who you are and why you're on your way. The monastery is old and small, but very well-maintained. The monks give you a room, but ask you not to go to sleep yet, but to participate in the Liturgy of the Hours with them. After matins, you retire to your cell, lent to you by the monks, expecting to depart the monastery tomorrow.
Time to sleep

The next day, you wake up and are invited to his home by the abbot of the monastery. He talks to you about your Le Pelerinage, curious about where you come from and where you're going. When you finish your conversation, he blesses you, and you leave the monastery. But when you stop, you wonder if it wouldn't be better to stay here and serve Dieu, not as a warrior and ruler, but as a simple monk, lower in the world than a worm, but greater in the Kingdom of Heaven.
No, that's not my calling
Maybe it is the right way
Lost Children

As you pass the forest, you see two children running towards you, shrilly calling out, "Pilgrim! Pilgrim! Stop!" When they run up, both children, distraught, tell you that while riding in a carriage with their parents and their friends, they were attacked by bandits, and they fled, unaware of their whereabouts or the location of their village. They tell you the name of the village, but unfortunately, the name means nothing to you.
I will help them
I don't have time. Life is cruel, they must found home independly than me...
Ruined caravan

You help the children and walk with them through the forest, sword at the ready. After a while, you reach the caravan the children spoke of. It's ruined, the horses are missing, and so is the cargo. You see the body of an old man, pierced by arrows. But that doesn't mean anything, because the parents might still be alive. You tell the children to stay where they are and go to look around...
I hope these children aren't orphans...
Parents

You look around and search for bodies. You find two other bodies, but one is a man in his 20s, and the other is a monk. After a moment, you think you see two silhouettes in the bushes. You call out to them, and they emerge: you see with your own eyes a man with a bushy beard and his wife with a bleeding leg. After a moment, you call out to the children, and they recognize the pair as their parents. You rejoice, because although many have died on the road, children are not orphans. Parents and children thank you wholeheartedly and promise to pray for you, and you slowly continue your journey.
I will also pray for them...
I'll return for a moment and donate them...

You look around and search for bodies. You find two other bodies, but one is a man in his 20s, and the other is a monk. A moment later, you find the body of a third man, even more riddled with arrows. He has a wedding ring on his hand
column3: he's probably the children's father. But suddenly, you see a woman in the bushes. You call out to him and tell him you're not a bandit. A middle-aged woman emerges from the bushes, wounded in the knee. You call out to the children, and they recognize her as their mother. You help the mother dress their wounds. You're happy that the children at least have a mother. You soon continue your journey, but you wonder if there's anything you can do for the children.

column2: I am poor pilgrim, I can't
I will donate them
I will take this wounded family into my court...

You look around and search for bodies. You find two other bodies, but one is a man in his 20s, and the other is a monk. After a while, you find the bodies of a third man and a woman, both wearing wedding rings. You know they are the children's parents. You don't call them, but you return to them and let them lead you to the village. There, you look for the house of their father's brother, whom they told you about on the way. Soon, you see him in the distance, talk to the man, and he agrees to take his brother's children in for raising. You wonder if there's anything you can do for these children...
I can't, because I am too poor....
I will donate them
I will take this poor children into my court...

You come across some peasants singing a strange song about Saint Louis the Martyr. You wonder if it's about the king beheaded by the Jacobins before the Event or about Louis Laflamme. You intend to listen to the song from behind the bushes, but the peasants notice you and recognize you as a stranger, then call out to you to join them.
Saint Louis the Martyr

You join the peasants. You reveal that you are on your own Le Pelerinage and are journeying to a sacred place. They greet you even more cheerfully and begin to tell you the story of Saint Louis the Martyr. Saint Louis of whom they sang, was a just and merciful king of France who, out of love for the people, assembled the Estates General to enact good laws to replace archaic. However, the Jacobins, tempted by the demon Marianne, incited the people and caused them to storm the Louvre and lead the king and his wife, the holy martyr Marie Antoinette, to the guillotine. And as the martyr-king was about to bow his head, he said: "I die innocent of all the crimes laid to my charge. I pardon those who are the cause of my death, and I pray to Dieu that the blood you are about to shed may never fall on France." Since then, St. Louis has been the patron saint of people who have difficulty in making decisions as well as of those who are kind, and as such, he is venerated by some peasants.
Nice story

When you finish listening to the story of Saint Louis the Martyr, the peasants sing another song about this king. You spend the rest of the day being entertained by the nearby peasants, given food and drink. The old men learn the songs of Saint Louis and only let you go after you recite one to them.
Nice people...
Along the way, he meets other travelers with the same goal as you, but to a different destination. You spend time together and pray, then go your separate ways.
